summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a text style.
description: `nonTextStyle(value)` is the same test as `!isTextStyle(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "TextStyle"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a text style; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
const style = SpreadsheetApp.newTextStyle().setBold(true).build();

nonTextStyle({}); // => true
nonTextStyle(null); // => true
nonTextStyle(style); // => false
```
